topics.name: Israel-Iran Conflict
topics.summary: New military conflict between Israel and Iran broke out; Wall Street Journal coverage discussed. Polymarket tracking 32% odds of US military action against Iran before July. Iran signaled interest in ceasefire. Tyler Cowen called the Israeli attack on Iranian nuclear facilities three months in advance.

topics.name: Meta Oakley Smart Glasses
topics.summary: Meta reportedly investing $5 billion for a 4% stake in Luxottica, which owns both Ray-Ban and Oakley. Hosts discussed Luxottica's dominance of the eyewear market as a strategic advantage for Meta to potentially corner iconic frame brands for its AR glasses roadmap.

topics.name: AlphaFold and AI for Science
topics.summary: John Jumper discussed AlphaFold's origin at DeepMind, how protein structure prediction went from a $100,000/year-long experiment to minutes of compute time. Discussed data efficiency improvements between AlphaFold 1 and 2, FDA adaptation challenges, and why the public markets did not significantly react to the breakthrough.

topics.name: Orphaned Horizontal SaaS Companies
topics.summary: Logan Bartlett and Christian Garrett discussed how $1-10 billion horizontal software companies are stuck between strategic acquirers focused on AI and private equity worried about AI disrupting their investments. Companies like Asana and Bill.com cited as examples trading at depressed multiples.

topics.name: Semi-Liquid Mega-Cap Private Companies
topics.summary: Christian Garrett described a new sub-asset class of 10-20 private companies (SpaceX, Stripe, Anduril, OpenAI, etc.) that are growing 50-100%, extremely profitable, and running liquid secondary markets, making them function almost like public stocks.

topics.name: Stablecoins and Circle IPO
topics.summary: Aaron Frank discussed the Circle IPO, stablecoin investment thesis, dollarization trends, the Genius Act, competitive dynamics between issuers and distribution players, and why the middle layer will get squeezed. Debated geopolitical risks of stablecoin adoption in non-friendly countries.

topics.name: Chime IPO
topics.summary: Aaron Frank discussed Chime's successful IPO below 2021 marks but up ~40% from IPO price. Seen as a positive catalyst for neobanking liquidity events and future M&A/aggregation by Chime itself.

topics.name: Venture Market Dynamics and Bill Gurley's State of the Union
topics.summary: Christian Garrett discussed Gurley's warnings about 2021 overhang with zombie unicorns, loss of singles/doubles in venture due to fund size growth, capital wars (referencing Uber vs. Lyft), and the need for M&A consolidation to work through excess inventory.

topics.name: Founding Engineer Meme
topics.summary: Viral meme about founding engineers taking on near-founder risk but getting a fraction of the equity and none of the status. Hosts argued the title matters less than actual financial outcome, and that being a founding engineer at a great company beats being a mediocre founder.

topics.name: AI Agents in Enterprise SaaS
topics.summary: Discussed how scaled SaaS incumbents (Intercom, ServiceNow, Salesforce) are launching their own agents with mixed results. Debated whether net-new agentic startups can compete given incumbent distribution advantages, and whether incumbents will gate core data to force agent usage.

topics.name: GLP-1 Drugs and Novo Nordisk Patent Failure
topics.summary: Novo Nordisk failed to pay a $450 patent maintenance fee on Ozempic, potentially giving Eli Lilly two additional years of competitive advantage. Hosts discussed the GLP-1 drug category's origins from Gila monster research.

topics.name: Pop Mart Mystery Box Phenomenon
topics.summary: Chinese toy company Pop Mart, worth $20-40 billion on the Hong Kong exchange, has built a massive business selling mystery box collectible toys. Stock up ~100% in the year. Hosts compared it to the mystery box economics of Pokemon card packs.

topics.name: ESG Investing Trends
topics.summary: Joseph Kass discussed how ESG was dominant in 2021-2022 but is no longer pushed to the front by institutional investors. The ESG brand has faded but sustainability conversations continue to grow in volume.

topics.name: Coinbase Military Parade Sponsorship
topics.summary: Coinbase was the presenting sponsor of the US Army's 250th anniversary parade. Hosts debated the irony of crypto (a libertarian technology) sponsoring the military, and whether it is appropriate for the Army to sell sponsorships.

topics.name: Waymo Premium Pricing
topics.summary: Waymo rides are costing more than Uber and Lyft but people are paying anyway. Discussed as evidence that automation with on-par or better reliability than humans commands a price premium.

topics.name: Robotics Investment Landscape
topics.summary: Christian Garrett discussed the robotics category with caution, noting it still feels on the R&D risk side especially for humanoid robots. Cited concerns about parallels to early autonomous vehicle hype cycles.

topics.name: Wildfire Detection Technology
topics.summary: Pano raised $44M Series B for wildfire early detection using computer vision and smart cameras. Anduril's abandoned wildfire-fighting autonomous tank project was discussed. Demand for 4K camera footage of fire origins highlighted.

topics.name: FinTech Bundling and Compound Startups
topics.summary: Debated why no one has built a single consumer neobank offering checking, savings, stocks, crypto, mortgage, and auto loan. Aaron Frank argued the barrier is product marketing fit, not product market fit or technology. Christian Garrett discussed compound startup strategies.

topics.name: AI Career Advice for New Graduates
topics.summary: Reid Hoffman's post discussed; argument is to AI-optimize careers rather than AI-proof them. Hosts drew analogies to internet-proofing in 1997 and YouTube-proofing in 2008, concluding the key is riding the wave rather than avoiding disruption.

topics.name: Politics and Portfolio Allocation
topics.summary: Wall Street Journal reporting discussed showing Democrats are more bearish and Republicans more bullish on the market based on party in the White House, contrary to the adage of keeping politics out of portfolios.

topics.name: Chess.com Growth
topics.summary: Chess.com grew from 35 million to 100 million accounts between June 2020 and December 2022, after taking 14 years to reach 35 million. ARR over $100 million. Highlighted as a pick-one-thing-and-dominate success story.
